title: [RFC][docs] Add viable/strict-blocking jobs one-pager
body: Document what viable/strict is, the blocking-set requirements (Failures % thresholds, pull runtime budget), core non-unstable jobs, and how to test new jobs / mark jobs unstable.

items.body: Part of https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/8281

+
+# viable/strict CI jobs
+## Background
+The [*viable/strict*](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/viable/strict) branch ensures all essential PyTorch tests are passing on it. This provides a stable base for contributions and greatly increases confidence that test failures are newly introduced. *viable/strict* should closely track *main*, providing a topline read on trunk health.
+
+All merged commits on main are candidates for becoming the new *viable/strict* head. Tests that must pass for this promotion to succeed are part of the *viable/strict*-blocking set. These tests must be high signal and minimally flaky. No subset of these tests should dominate advancement failures.
+
+## Blocking Set Requirements
+The *viable/strict*-blocking set is encompassed by `trunk`, `pull`, `lint`, and `docs-build`. Jobs that are part of these workflows should meet the following requirements:
+
+Let **Failures %** (given a job, over an N-day window) be defined as the percent of commits where this job was red, over the decided main commits in the provided window.
+1. A job should only be added to the *viable/strict*-blocking set if it meets **Failures % less than 10% over the last 7 days**. Furthermore, jobs added to the frequently-run `pull` workflow should not cause `pull` runtime to exceed 90 minutes. The job owner is responsible for ensuring these requirements are met.

items.author: georgehong
items.body:
It looks like L3 is setting a 10% threshold for failures? 
> | Job pass rate | > 90% | At least 90% of CI jobs should succeed. This is a **job-level** metric, not a test-level metric. |

Some of our long-term stable jobs also spike, even in a 7-day window, if a CI SEV happens or a true test regression is introduced, so I feel like starting with less strict constraints could help.

items.author: georgehong
items.body:
Yes, this definitely has a huge effect on making the automation fair too. The 7-day window was meant to address some of this, since it should smooth out brief failure sequences. GH sevs and viable/strict blockages > 24 hours definitely propagate up to these metrics, even our very reliable ones. I think we can address this in two ways:
1. We can make removal from viable/strict set conservative. If either of the above outage events have occurred in the window, we can keep jobs in. Flakiness/unreliability shouldn't cause the same degree of outages and tend to be more independent.
2. We can allow for exclusion of certain days in the 7-day window. Given the importance of viable/strict, it seems reasonable to also wait for a clean window, but we can grant exceptions in the above outage cases.

items.author: huydhn
items.body:
What I mean is that there is an alternative / complementary approach of using a fixed threshold like 10% which is to use relative threshold, let's say 5%. For example, if the p50 of pull workflow failures in main is, let's say, 50%, adding a job with the failure rate of 55% is kind of ok-ish if it shares the same failures as the rest.

You're right, however, that it would further lower the overall success rate, so it might be a bad idea and make thing more complicated.

+# viable/strict CI Jobs
+## Background
+The [*viable/strict*](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/viable/strict) branch ensures all essential PyTorch tests are passing on it. This provides a stable base for contributions and greatly increases confidence that test failures are newly introduced. *viable/strict* should closely track *main*, providing a topline read on trunk health.
+
+All merged commits on *main* are candidates for becoming the new *viable/strict* head. Tests that must pass for this promotion to succeed are part of the *viable/strict*-blocking set. These tests must be high signal and minimally flaky. No subset of these tests should dominate advancement failures.
+
+## Blocking Set Requirements
+The *viable/strict*-blocking set is drawn from the *trunk*, *pull*, *lint*, and *docs-build* workflows. Jobs that are part of these workflows should meet the following requirements:
+
+Let **Failures %** (given a job, over an N-day window) be defined as the percent of commits where this job was red, over the decided (non-pending) *main* commits in the provided window.
+1. A job should only be added to the *viable/strict*-blocking set if it meets **Failures % less than 10% over the last 7 days**, viewable on the HUD [*reliability* page](https://hud.pytorch.org/reliability), or computed manually on [the trunk dashboard](https://hud.pytorch.org/hud/pytorch/pytorch/main).
